Features

Simulation is performed according to the following rules that apply to all profile time slices that are assigned to a time-of-use rate
in the simulation period:

Zero values in disconnection period

synthetic profile adjusted to

billed annual consumption

synthetic profile adjusted to
period consumption of interval meter

Time-of-Use Simulation Rules for Externally Saved Profile Values

Step 1: Zero Values in Disconnection Period

The billing program checks whether the interval meter has been disconnected during the simulation period. The system observes

disconnections with the disconnection statuses 02 - Lowered/lLimited and03 - Disconnected. It is assumed that the
disconnection period has zero consumption, meaning that the profile values are set to zero.

Step 2: Adjust Synthetic Profile to Measured Annual Consumption

For the remaining simulation period, the system uses a synthetic profile to generate the profile values. The synthetic profile is
determined using the consumption pattern specified in the time-of-use interface. The synthetic profile has a standardized annual

consumption and therefore has to be adjusted to the annual consumption of the customer. The billing program attempts to
determine the measured annual consumption for the profile by aggregating the existing measured total consumptions from MDUS
requests. The system uses MDUS requests from the representative period according to the percentage minimum share in the rate.
Changes to the period consumption mean that consumptions from MDUS requests from older periods are not used.

1 Note

You can use the method DETERMINE_CONTRACTS in the BADI ISU_FASTEDM_TOU_SIMULATION to influence the contract
periods from which MDUS requests can be observed.

Aggregation of the total consumption from MDUS requests does not have to take place for an entire year, but is based ona
percentage minimum share in the rate. The synthetic profile is also used for the extrapolation of aggregated consumption values
for a year.
